# gladvn UI - AI Guidelines

You are an AI Coding Assistant helping a developer use the `gladvn` UI library.
`gladvn` is a CLI-first React component library built on top of **Base UI (`@base-ui/react`)** and **Tailwind CSS v4**, featuring a strict **Micro (Primitives) / Macro (Presets)** architecture and **Zero-Portal Scoped Theme Tunneling**.

## 1. Installation & CLI Usage
- Use `npx gladvn init` to scaffold the library, CSS tokens (`tokens.css` + `gladvn.css`), and `@gladvn` path aliases into a project.
- Use `npx gladvn add <component>` or `npx gladvn add-block <block>` to add individual components or blocks.
- **NEVER** use `npm install gladvn`. Components are copied directly into the project's source code under the `@gladvn` alias (default: `./gladvn/`).

### Import Guidelines
- **ALWAYS** import components using the configured `@gladvn` alias path:
  - **Micro Primitives (Barrel):** `import { Button, Card, Dialog } from "@gladvn"`
  - **Micro Primitives (Deep):** `import { Button } from "@gladvn/components/micro/button"`
  - **Macro Presets (Barrel):** `import { InputPreset, SelectPreset, DialogPreset } from "@gladvn/preset"`
  - **Macro Presets (Deep):** `import { InputPreset } from "@gladvn/components/macro/input-preset"`
  - **Incorrect:** `import { Button } from "gladvn"`

## 2. Micro vs. Macro Architecture (Selection Hierarchy)
1. **Macro First (Presets):** For standard forms, dialogs, selects, comboboxes, and cards, prefer Macro presets (`@gladvn/preset`). They encapsulate common state, validation, accessibility (`useId`, `aria-invalid`), and layout while composing Micro primitives under the hood.
2. **Micro Second (Primitives):** When custom layout or fine-grained slot composition is needed, assemble UI using stateless Micro primitives (`@gladvn`).

```tsx
// ✅ Macro — Ready-to-use preset with label, description, error & adornments
import { InputPreset } from "@gladvn/preset";

<InputPreset
  label="Email Address"
  placeholder="name@example.com"
  errorMessage={errors.email?.message}
/>

// ✅ Micro — Pure composition when custom structure is needed
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardContent } from "@gladvn";

<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Hello World</CardTitle>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>
    Some content here.
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

**Incorrect (Do not hallucinate configuration props on Micro primitives):**
```tsx
// ❌ DO NOT DO THIS on Micro Card (use CardPreset instead)
<Card title="Hello World" content="Some content here" />
```

## 3. Form Fields (Micro Composition)
When building custom forms with Micro primitives instead of `FieldPreset` / `InputPreset`, use the `Field` family to handle accessibility, labels, and error messages:
```tsx
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldContent, FieldError, Input } from "@gladvn";

<Field invalid={!!errors.email}>
  <FieldLabel>Email Address</FieldLabel>
  <FieldContent>
    <Input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" aria-invalid={!!errors.email} />
  </FieldContent>
  <FieldError>{errors.email?.message}</FieldError>
</Field>
```

## 4. Styling, Colors & Variants
- Components support **9 semantic colors**: `primary`, `secondary`, `destructive`, `warning`, `success`, `info`, `tertiary`, `muted`, `accent`.
- Interactive components (like `Button`, `Badge`, `Alert`) support **5 variants**: `solid`, `outline`, `soft`, `ghost`, `link`.
- Sizes follow standard tokens: `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
- Pass Tailwind CSS v4 utility classes via `className` to extend or position components:
  `<Button className="w-full" variant="solid" color="primary">Submit</Button>`

## 5. Polymorphism (`render` prop)
- Most interactive components are powered by **Base UI** and use the `render` prop (instead of Radix's `asChild`) for element delegation:
  ```tsx
  <Button render={<a href="/dashboard" />}>Go to Dashboard</Button>
  ```

## 6. Overlay Components & Zero-Portal Theming
- Overlay components (`Dialog`, `Confirm`, `Sheet`, `Drawer`, `Popover`, `Tooltip`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `DropdownMenu`, `ContextMenu`, `HoverCard`, `NavigationMenu`) use portals and automatically inherit scoped `.light` / `.dark` themes from `ThemeProvider` via built-in `ThemeWrapper` (`display: contents`). Do **not** wrap overlay contents in manual theme wrappers.
```tsx
import { Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, Button } from "@gladvn";

<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Title</DialogTitle>
    </DialogHeader>
    Content
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

## 7. Icons
`gladvn` relies on standard SVG icons (such as `lucide-react`). Components automatically size direct SVG icons using zero-specificity selectors (`[:where(&_svg)]`), so you can pass `<Icon />` without manual size classes or override them freely with `className="size-5"`.

---
*Note to AI: Always prioritize reading the TypeScript types of the imported components in `@gladvn` and `@gladvn/preset` if you are unsure of the props.*
